newsitem.title: USA: Short covering lifts CME lumber to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Short covering lifts CME lumber to higher close.

text.p: Short covering developed early and CME lumber futures ended higher in an expanded trading limit that followed two days of limit losses, traders said.

January had posted limit losses Tuesday and Wednesday which resulted in the expanded $15.00 per thousand board foot limits. But selling lacked follow through and prices surged as futures were holding too large a discount to cash. Seasonal factors are also starting to point higher as mills trim production during winter holidays, they said.
Futures closed $9.60 to $3.40 higher with January up $5.70 at $380.50 and March up $6.40 at $371.20 per tbf.

Futures eased to the level that cash markets are expected to retreat to from recent highs. Cash spruce prices have tumbled over $55 since last week and are seen moving below $400, possibly down to $380, as they correct from the sharp advance earlier this month, traders said.
"We are as close to cash as we have been in a long, long time," one trader said.

The early rally ran into fund liquidation which took futures down to technical support before rallying again. The market held a trend line at the day's lows and it now also looks technically stronger, they said.
